video_title: Clippers finalize delayed Kawhi trade to Raptors + Concerns for Knicks & Heat 👀 | Get Up

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Kawhi Leonard trade puts Raptors in Eastern Conference contender conversation
quotes.excerpt: It puts them in the conversation with some of the top teams in the East.
quotes.quote: It puts them in the conversation with some of the top teams in the East. Certainly where New York is right now, I think they are a little bit of a step above everyone else, but it was an arms race this summer when you look at what Philadelphia was able to do with Jaylen Brown and LeBron James, and Giannis Antetokounmpo going to Miami, Cleveland bringing back their group, Indiana will be in the mix again. They went from a good story last year that probably overachieved a bit to now pairing Kawhi Leonard with Scotty Barnes and RJ Barrett and having three big wings there.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Raptors face high risk with Kawhi Leonard's injury history
quotes.excerpt: You can't trust him to be on the court. That's the risk that the Raptors are taking.
quotes.quote: Three of the last nine seasons has he played at least 60 games. You can't trust him to be on the court. That's the risk that the Raptors are taking here. This is a high-risk, potentially high-reward type of deal. You hope that Kawhi can be healthy come playoff time. The risk is that he's not going to be available, and you're paying him a lot of money. You gave up a lot to get him.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' biggest hurdle is frontcourt depth after losing Mitchell Robinson
quotes.excerpt: When you lose Mitchell Robinson to Boston as a free agent, do you have enough frontcourt size?
quotes.quote: I think frontcourt size is the biggest thing. When you lose Mitchell Robinson to Boston as a free agent, and then you still have Carl-Anthony Towns and you signed Andre Drummond and you have Mohamed Bamba here, do you have enough frontcourt size with this Knicks group who are in the top five in points in the paint and second-chance points? That would be the big concern with me.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' championship run was a result of perfect timing
quotes.excerpt: This is a team that peaked at the perfect time.
quotes.quote: This is a team that peaked at the perfect time. Everything came together at the exact time they needed to last year. I don't think they're going to be some 65 or 70-win juggernaut. There will be ups and downs again in the regular season, just like there were last year. But if the Knicks don't repeat, I don't think it's because they got fat and happy. This is a mature team. Jalen Brunson, their leader, is even-keeled as they come.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: 76ers' championship pedigree is key to building good chemistry
quotes.excerpt: Jaylen Brown and LeBron James have already won championships. The other three players haven't.
quotes.quote: They have some championship pedigree. Jaylen Brown and LeBron James have already won championships. The other three players haven't, and I think that's going to be the needed recipe here. Offensively, it's going to be as dynamic as any team. Usage rate is going to be a little bit of a concern because they're going to have to share the basketball. Some of these players are ball-dominant here, and defensively, can they get stops at the end of games? If there's anything, it's basically where is Joel Embiid when we get to April?

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Skepticism regarding 76ers' fit and usage rates
quotes.excerpt: I'm a Sixers skeptic because you are relying on a guy who is about to turn 42.
quotes.quote: I'm a Sixers skeptic because you are relying on a guy who is about to turn 42 and a big man you hope plays 42 games. I am concerned about the fit. This is a phenomenal fantasy basketball lineup. I don't know how it fits together. How does that get spliced up? Do these guys enhance each other, or is it my turn, your turn, his turn, his turn? And then just style of play. This is a team that one through four is suited to play 100 miles an hour, but you've got four Ferraris and a Winnebago in the starting lineup.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Heat lack championship-level playmaking despite adding Clay Thompson
quotes.excerpt: I'm not ready to put them as a championship-level team right now.
quotes.quote: I don't think they are. I think it was a need that was needed just based on this was a perennial team that was in the play-in right now. When you have Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam together, the question for me is there enough playmakers on the court? Is there going to be enough spacing? They added Clay Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr. Remember, a lot of the playmaking last year was with Tyler Herro at the end of games. Do they have a shot creator here? I think they're better than where they are, but I'm not ready to put them as a championship-level team right now.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Heat face spacing and playmaking challenges outside of Giannis
quotes.excerpt: Outside of Giannis, there's a real lack of playmaking.
quotes.quote: I've got real concerns about the fit. Bam will shoot threes, but he's not a threat from three-point range. Giannis is obviously best when the floor is spaced, when he's attacking downhill. A Brook Lopez type of big who spaces the floor is what fits best with him. So I'm not saying that can't work, but it's going to take some time, some tinkering, some trial and error by Eric Spoelstra and those guys to figure it out. This is a team that outside of Giannis, there's a real lack of playmaking.
